Iron ore entering 'bloodletting' phase, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX

sectors.trend: Sharp decline; iron ore 'bloodletting' underway, cap raises signal distress, gold underperforming ('schmould')
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin pressure; smaller miners (Crucible, Kuniko, Gateway WA) raising capital in weak tape; gold miners (GOLD.AX, NVG.AX) lack safe-haven bid

sectors.trend: Banks dragging ASX lower amid growth scare and rising bond yields; Queensland downgrade raises sovereign credit concerns
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX under pressure from credit-risk repricing; QLD downgrade may affect state-linked lending exposure

sectors.trend: Oil near US$100 on failed suppression; Australia softens gas reservation rules; Santos preservation signals policy shift
sectors.implications: Santos (STO.AX), Woodside (WDS.AX) benefit from eased gas rules; oil-linked names (Woods Point, Oil Search) supported; but higher input costs hit downstream

sectors.trend: Woolworths breaches own 'Price Freeze' on staples; businesses cite tax burden and demand softness
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WOW.AX face margin squeeze and reputational risk; consumer spending under pressure from tax load and housing correction

sectors.trend: High-end housing prices in steepest falls; affordable segment resilient; RBA focused on rental inflation; property chiefs call for more migration
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) face mixed rental dynamics; developers (MRG.AX, DHG.AX) benefit from first-home buyer surge but face construction cost pressures

sectors.trend: Austal.AX jumps on US$1.9b bid; Critical Resources battery tech passes month-long test; AI/tech themes active globally
sectors.implications: Austal.AX (AUS.AX) M&A catalyst; battery/energy-storage names gain credibility; limited ASX-listed pure-play tech exposure

key_themes: Commodity super-cycle reversal: iron ore bloodletting and gold weakness signal peak-cycle concerns
AUD weakness amplifies import inflation, complicating RBA's rental-inflation dilemma
Energy policy pivot: gas reservation easing and Santos preservation reshape Australia's export posture
Housing bifurcation: luxury correction vs affordable resilience; first-home buyer surge
Mining sector capital stress: cap raises in a falling market signal liquidity risk
Sovereign credit risk: Queensland downgrade a bellwether for state fiscal sustainability
Superannuation policy debate: One Nation populism vs institutional stability

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Iron ore price collapse / commodity demand shock
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce materials weight; hedge via energy and consumer staples; monitor Chinese inflation data (#52) as demand proxy
Favour domestic-revenue companies; avoid import-heavy retailers; watch RBA commentary on rental inflation
Avoid small-cap miners raising capital in weak tape; focus on cash-flow-positive majors
Monitor QLD and other state bond spreads; reduce exposure to state-linked infrastructure plays
Maintain energy allocation as hedge; keep cash buffer; avoid over-leveraged positions
Differentiate luxury vs affordable segments; favour REITs with rental income over speculative developers

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid small-cap miners raising capital in weak tape

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain defensive consumer staples allocation but monitor WES margin risk

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to extend weakness over 1–3 months as iron ore correction deepens, AUD remains under pressure, and RBA navigates rental inflation without cutting. Oil near US$100 provides energy support but broad-based risk-off persists. Expect elevated volatility around US-Iran geopolitical developments.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautiously constructive if commodity prices stabilise and RBA eases. Housing correction at high end may stabilise by H2 2027. Energy policy shifts (gas, Santos) support structural earnings. Mining recovery contingent on Chinese demand; superannuation policy clarity needed to restore investor confidence.
